fills.researcher_notes: CONFIRMS the sheet's existing 53.14 km, does not change it. SNGPL's own live 'Province-Wise Transmission Breakup' page (What We Do > Transmission System) is a text table of every named transmission line by diameter with length in km. Row 16 reads verbatim '|16|QADIRPUR LINE|36|53.14|' -- diameter AND length both match this row exactly (36in / 53.14km). This is the highest-value find flagged in the protocol: a text-searchable SNGPL asset register, not a map. RECONCILES the sweep's earlier single-source concern (staged in ref-sweep-operating/rows/P4088.json) that an independent 2006 Emerson/PSIG SNGPL network paper (S.R. Lone & R.P. Spiers, 'Gas Transmission Development Strategy', https://www.emerson.com/is/content/emerson/it/final-control/documents/d352531x012.pdf -- content independently re-verified here via `pdftotext -layout` since url_verifier's substring match false-negatives on this PDF's compressed streams, a documented false-negative for this file per the prior researcher's note) gives 'Qadirpur gas is transported to Bhong via a 44-mile 36-inch pipeline' (44mi=70.81km), ~25% longer than 53.14km. The SAME SNGPL breakup table also lists a SEPARATE line item, row 40: '|40|QADIRPUR  - AC-1X LINE|36|16.88|' -- AC-1X is literally the Bhong compressor-station complex named in the Emerson paper ('Bhong compressor station (AC1X)'/'AC1XQ'). Summing the two named SNGPL segments at the same 36in diameter: 53.14 + 16.88 = 70.02 km, within 0.79 km (1.1%) of Emerson's 70.81 km. The same pattern holds for the sibling 30in line (QADIRPUR LINE 30in=53.13 + QADIRPUR-AC1X LINE 30in=17.11 = 70.24km, vs Emerson's stated '44-mile 30-inch pipeline' for that line too). This means the two sources do NOT actually disagree once granularity is accounted for: Emerson's 44 miles describes the FULL Qadirpur-to-Bhong-compressor-station corridor; GEM's P4088 row (and this SNGPL line item) covers only the first, longer named segment of that corridor, with SNGPL's separate 'AC-1X LINE' item covering the final ~17km tie-in into the compressor station. LengthKnown=53.14 is therefore well-supported for the row as GEM has scoped it. tier=high because two independent sources (current SNGPL register + 2006 Emerson paper), read at the correct granularity, triangulate to the same physical reality.
